intent: Final iteration: revert to the iteration 8 geometry, the best-evidenced design (939.3, 60/60 completions). This reverses the iteration 10 wheel_radius increase, which cut slalom finishes from 20/20 to 12/20, and keeps the sensor footprint at 0.012 m, which the iteration 9 test showed is best. The aim is a robust platform for the unseen final track. The Integrator should keep the controller tuned to the iteration 8 geometry and check kd, since the track change of iteration 8 is the most recent tuning reference.
learning: Iteration 10 showed that a larger wheel (0.044 m) helps the oval's completion time but breaks slalom finishes, so wheel_radius is not a free speed lever on alternating bends. Iteration 9 showed that a larger sensor footprint blurs the signal on the sharpest bends. Together these mean the iteration 8 geometry sits near the best trade-off available in this design space. Next, check whether the final design's slalom finishes hold at 20/20 and whether line_loss_events stay near 1 per run. If the Integrator reports that the controller can absorb a slightly larger wheel, the remaining gain is in completion_time, but this is the final iteration, so no further geometry change is tested here.
rationale: Iteration 10 scored 864.9, below the iteration 8 best of 939.3. Its only change was wheel_radius 0.040 to 0.044 m. That helped the oval (completion_time 1.85 to 1.67 s) but broke the slalom: finishes fell from 20/20 to 12/20, with 8 off_track endings and mean slalom score 701. The larger wheel raised turn rate per unit of wheel differential, and the slalom's alternating bends showed it first. Across iterations 3 to 8, every agility step that held the slalom together (lower mass, shorter body, narrower body, narrower track) raised or kept slalom progress, while the wheel-radius increase in iteration 10 reversed that. Iteration 9 also showed that a 0.016 m sensor footprint hurts slalom finishes, so sensor_size stays at 0.012 m. The evidence therefore favours the iteration 8 geometry, which completed 60/60 development trials with rms_error 0.0056 to 0.0099 m and progress of 0.996 to 0.998. Because the final score comes from an unseen track of a different shape, a design with 60/60 completions on known tracks is worth more than an untested compromise such as wheel_radius 0.042 m, which could land in the slalom failure zone. I am reverting wheel_radius to 0.040 m and keeping every other value from iteration 8. Expected result: about 939 on the development tracks, with completions held at 60/60 and slalom finishes near 20/20.
